Accent, buttons, FAB

Route 3: the green stops being the button colour and goes back to meaning fuel
ANSWERS  your note on sheets 01–07
READS    spec §D3 one green · §D7
PALETTE  sheet 01 · icons sheet 02b
DATE     2026-08-03
THE DIAGNOSIS

The accent was carrying two unrelated jobs

§D3 sets accent === domain.fuel — one green in the app. But the batch-1 sheets also used that green for every primary button, every FAB, every back link and every ✓. So the same pixel meant fuel money and press this, and because a button is a solid block, "press this" won.

That is the same failure the icon wells had. The fix there was to stop saturated blocks being the heaviest object on screen. This is that fix applied to actions.

THE RULE, AFTER
Emphasis is ink. A primary action is the darkest object on the surface, not the greenest.
The accent means fuel. Wells, bars, dots, the fuel tile. Nothing else.
One exception, deliberate: tinted interactive text — back links, toast actions, sheet affordances — stays accent. It is type, not a block, so it reads as tappable without competing for weight. See §04.

This costs no spec amendment. §D3 asked for one green; it now has exactly one meaning too.

Recommendation: 8px, and the reasoning is not taste

Koi is an iOS-native product using native sheets, native keyboards and native nav bars. Fully square corners fight that chrome — the platform's own controls are round-rectangles, and a square button next to a rounded system sheet reads as a rendering bug, not as a style. But 11px is the radius of a consumer app that wants to feel friendly, and this product's voice is a quiet ledger.

8px is soft enough to belong on iOS and tight enough to read as a document. It also has a real relationship to the icon wells: the well is 10px on a 40px box; 8px on a 44px button gives the same ratio, so buttons and wells are now the same family instead of two independent guesses. On the Industry chrome that documents these sheets, corners stay square — the chrome and the product are allowed to disagree, because one is a spec sheet and one is an app.

Recommendation: C — ink squircle, 52px, neutral shadow

Three reasons. Ink because + creates any record — a green FAB promises a fuel fill and delivers a chooser with six tiles, five of which are not fuel. 52px because 58 was sized to compete with a coloured shadow it no longer has; 52 still clears the 44pt target with room, and the object stops being the loudest thing on a calm screen. Neutral shadow because a coloured shadow is a glow, and §D7 has no glows.

The squircle (16px on 52) rather than a circle: it matches the 8px button family and the 10px wells at the same ratio, so the FAB reads as the same species of object as everything else rather than as a platform convention bolted on. Rejected: E — an outlined FAB is too quiet for the one control that must always be findable, and a translucent fill over a scrolling ledger stops being legible exactly when the list gets dense.

THE DARK PRIMARY IS THE LIGHTEST OBJECT

"Emphasis is ink" inverts correctly: in dark, ink is the near-white, so the primary is the brightest thing on the surface. That is why this rule survives the theme flip where a coloured primary would need a second hue authored for dark.

04 · The knock-ons — what else was green

Five things in batch 1 used the accent and were not fuel. Each needs a ruling, not a sweep.
Option chips → INK
Petrol Diesel Electric

The only case where accent filled a shape for a non-fuel reason — and on the fuel sheet it put a green Petrol chip beside a green fuel well meaning two different things. Selected is now an ink hairline plus a real check glyph, so selection is carried by mark and weight, not hue.

Picker ✓ STAYS ACCENT
Cost
Fuel
Distance

A bare glyph on a hairline row, never a fill. It is the iOS convention for "this is the chosen one" and carries no weight — the row's text is what you read. Changing it would cost clarity and gain nothing.

Back links STAYS ACCENT
Garage Golf GTI Edit
Discard · Save · Cancel all read the same way

Tinted type in a nav bar is the platform's own signal for "tappable", and it is the one place users look without being told. Ink here would make Back look like a title.

Toast actions STAYS ACCENT
Reading deleted. Undo

Undo and Retry are the only actions allowed in a toast, they are time-boxed, and they must be reachable at a glance without shouting. Tinted type on a card that is already floating is exactly enough.

Filter chips ALREADY INK
All Fuel Service

Selected filters were ink-filled from the start, and that decision is now the model the option chips follow. Listed because it is the proof the pattern was already half-right — the inconsistency was the option chip, not this.

The line these five draw

Accent as a fill means fuel money — and now only that. Accent as tinted type or a hairline means "this responds to touch", which is the iOS convention the platform already teaches and which costs no visual weight. The option chip is the one that had to move: it was the only place the accent filled a shape for a reason that had nothing to do with fuel, and on the fuel sheet specifically it produced a green Petrol chip sitting beside a green fuel well meaning two different things.

This is the sheet that proves the rule. Before, the green wash on the two filled fields meant "you typed this", the green chip meant "selected", and the green Save meant "commit" — three meanings, one colour, on the fuel sheet where green already means fuel. After: filled fields take an ink hairline, the chip is ink-marked with a real check glyph, and Save is ink-weighted. Discard stays accent — it is tinted type, and the one thing that must never look like the primary.

The privacy card is where the old green was most wrong: a saturated green Turn on sync read as a marketing CTA on the one surface whose whole job is to be soberly factual. Ink is the right register. What gets sent › stays accent — tinted type, secondary, and it wants to be findable without being urged.

06 · What changes in the tokens

Additive. No existing hex moves, so nothing on sheet 01 is invalidated.
// ADD to palette.light / palette.dark — control surfaces
control: {
  primaryBg:    light '#1C1A17'  dark '#F4F0E8',   // === ink, both schemes
  primaryFg:    light '#FBF9F5'  dark '#14120F',   // === paper, both schemes
  primaryPress: light '#3B3733'  dark '#CFC8BC',
  secondaryBg:  light '#FFFFFF'  dark '#211E19',   // === card
  secondaryPress: light '#F2EFE8' dark '#2B2721',
  ghostPress:   light '#EEF3EC'  dark '#1E2A1B',   // === domainWash.fuel
  focusRing:    light '#43823B'  dark '#4E9139',   // === accent. the one exception
}

// ADD — shape scale, so buttons/wells/fields stop being independent guesses
radius: { field: 8, button: 8, well: 10, card: 15, sheet: 26, fab: 16, chip: 999 }

// ADD — the FAB, now a described object rather than an ad-hoc circle
fab: { size: 52, radius: 16, bg: 'control.primaryBg', fg: 'control.primaryFg',
       shadow: '0 6px 18px rgba(28,26,23,0.18)' }   // neutral. never a glow.

// UNCHANGED: every domain hue, every semantic, both grounds, the whole ink ramp.
// accent stays === domain.fuel. It simply stops appearing on control fills.

Why a radius scale is worth adding now

Batch 1 used 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18 and 26px across the sheets — eight radii, none of them related. Naming seven roles instead means the next screen inherits its corner rather than inventing one, which is the same argument as the token set itself.

One accessibility gain, free

The old primary was #FBF9F5 on #43823B — {{ oldPrimaryRatio }}, which clears AA for the 15px label but not by much. Ink-on-paper is {{ newPrimaryRatio }}. The most-pressed control in the app went from adequate to AAA.

What I did not touch

No open question in §16 is affected, and no spec article needs amending — this is a reading of §D3, not a change to it. The one thing worth your explicit blessing is the tinted-type exception in §04: it is the reason the app still looks like it has an accent at all.

Sheet 08 of 08. Say the word and I roll ink primary · 8px · FAB C through sheets 01–07 in one pass, then add the domainWash and radius ramps to sheet 01's token block. If you would rather a different radius or FAB, name it and I roll that instead — the sheets are the same amount of work either way.
